sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
11 Nissan 5731

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the name of the tribe Asher, its connection to Israel's praise and redemption, and raises questions about the nature of choice between Israel and G-d.

translations.translation: "On the eleventh day, the prince of the children of Asher [offered]."
And it is brought in the Midrash:
All the tribes were named for the sake of Israel's redemption and for their praise.
And Asher was named for the sake of Israel's redemption, as it is said:
"And all nations shall call you fortunate, for you shall be a desirable land, says the L-rd of Hosts."
And for their praise, as it is said:
"Fortunate is the people for whom it is so; fortunate is the people whose G-d is the L-rd."
The good fortune of Israel is only because they chose the Holy One, blessed be He, to be their G-d.
And the Holy One, blessed be He, chose them to be His treasured people.
Therefore, when the prince of Asher came to offer,
he offered his sacrifice regarding the choice that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose Israel from among all the nations,
as it is said:
"And the L-rd your G-d has chosen you to be His treasured people."
And it needs to be understood:
For at the beginning of the matter, it says that Israel's good fortune is that they chose the Holy One, blessed be He
(and that He then chose them seems to be an additional matter).
And afterwards it says that Asher
(for the name of Israel's good fortune)
offered his sacrifice regarding the choice that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose Israel.
Also, it needs to be understood:
Choice applies specifically to two things that are equal,
or where each has a virtue that the other lacks.
But regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, and, by contrast, the alien gods,
how can it be said that Israel chose the Holy One, blessed be He?
And similarly, regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, choosing Israel,
Israel is incomparably superior to all the nations,
so what is the meaning of the Holy One, blessed be He, choosing Israel?
Also, what is said in Tanya,
that "You have chosen us from every people and tongue" refers to the physical body, which in its materiality resembles the bodies of the nations of the world,
requires explanation,
for that the body of Israel resembles
(externally)
the bodies of the nations of the world is not an explanation
(apparently)
regarding the Holy One, blessed be He.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Midrashic parable of the king and the wise man, questioning why special cleverness is needed to choose the king over the changing officials.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is said,
"The L-rd is my portion, said my soul."
And it is brought in the Midrash:
A parable of a king who entered a province, and with him were dukes, governors, and generals, etc.
One said, "I will take the dukes for myself"; another said, "I will take the governors for myself"; another said, "I will take the generals for myself."
There was one clever person there who said, "I will take the king for myself, for all of them are replaceable, but the king is not replaceable."
So too, the nations of the world—some worship the sun, some worship the moon, etc., but Israel worships only the Holy One, blessed be He.
Thus it is said, "The L-rd is my portion, said my soul."
And the precise point in this is known,
for apparently,
even one who is not clever, and even a small child,
knows that the king is greater than the dukes, etc.
So why is cleverness needed to choose the king?
And also,
even if the dukes, etc., were not replaceable, it would be simply understood that the king is greater than them.
[And especially according to what is known
in the explanation of the verse,
"From his shoulder and upward he was taller than all the people,"
that even the shoulder of the king,
meaning the attributes that are drawn from the intellect of the head and below it,
is higher than the head
(the intellect)
of all the people,
in which
(all the people)
are included even the greatest ministers],
so why
is the reason needed that "all of them are replaceable"?
